newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo airline JAT to modernise fleet -paper.
newsitem.headline: Yugo airline JAT to modernise fleet -paper.

text.p: Yugoslav flag air carrier Jugoslovenski Aerotransport (JAT)'s board of directors has endorsed a programme of modernisation of 17 planes from its fleet, Belgrade newspaper Politika reported on Tuesday.
Under the programme, nine DC-9s and eight Boeing 727s will have new engines and navigation systems installed which will extend their flight life by 15 years, the report said.
The modernisation of 17 of JAT's total fleet of 30 planes, to be carried out in the national airline's hangars, will cost an estimated $80 million.

The company has proposed that, besides funds set aside by JAT, the fleet modernisation be financed with a credit from the Serbian Development Fund, arguing it will contribute to developing tourism and international air transport.

The Serbian Development Fund, the sole recipient of funds from the sale last month of a 49 percent stake in Serbia's telecom company to Italian and Greek partners, has started approving credits for export-oriented production.
The modernised planes will be able to fly to all airports in Europe since their new engines will not produce so much noise, the report said.

"Forthcoming stricter noise regulations threaten to exclude JAT's DC-9s and 727s from major European airports, which is why the airline is embarking on this costly noise reduction programme," an industry analyst told Reuters.
